newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Feb trade surplus rises to 9.2 bln DM.
newsitem.headline: German Feb trade surplus rises to 9.2 bln DM.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus rose to 9.2 billion marks ($5.3 billion) in February from 5.6 billion marks the month before, and from 8.4 billion marks in February 1996, the Federal Statistics Office said on Tuesday.

The current account, which includes trade in services as well as goods, showed a deficit of 1.5 billion marks, narrowing sharply from 9.8 billion marks in January. The current account was in surplus by 0.6 billion marks in February 1996.

Exports rose to 67.8 billion marks from 64.4 billion marks in January and from 62.9 billion marks a year earlier, while imports were 58.6 billion marks, down from 58.8 billion marks in January but up from 54.5 billion a year earlier.
The services account was in deficit by 4.1 billion marks, compared with a 5.6 billion mark gap in January and 2.4 billion marks a year earlier.

For the first two months of 1997, Germany's trade surplus was 14.8 billion marks, up from 13.0 billion marks in the same period of 1996, while the current account deficit was 11.2 billion marks, jumping from 3.4 billion marks.
